title: How to Setup the Jina AI MCP Server in 2026
summary: Jina AI MCP integration allows developers to bridge the gap between static training data and live internet information for more accurate responses.
body_markdown:
## Requirements and costs for running Jina AI MCP


Operationalizing the Jina AI MCP server requires an active Jina Reader API key to authenticate requests between your local environment and the web-scraping backend.


### The Jina Reader API credit system explained house prices


To prevent a single runaway agent from saturating the global scraping pool, Jina AI uses a tiered credit system to manage high-concurrency access to its web-parsing infrastructure.


**10 million tokens** are provided in the free tier as initial headroom for you to test workflows without an immediate financial commitment. The infrastructure supports a 100 billion daily token capacity so that high-volume research tasks don't hit an abrupt wall.


**$0.02 per million tokens** is the cost for Embeddings V5 Text Nano to provide a low-cost entry point for vectorizing scraped content, which means developers can process massive datasets without significant budgetary constraints.


Embeddings V5 Omni Small costs $0.05 per million tokens to balance cost and semantic precision for more demanding reasoning tasks, so users gain higher accuracy while maintaining manageable operational expenses.


Your research agent moves from a single-user Claude Sonnet 5.5 instance to a department-wide deployment with predictable costs, meaning organizations can scale their AI infrastructure without the risk of fluctuating monthly bills.


### Setting up the server in Claude Desktop or Cursor


Configuring the MCP server involves modifying the local configuration file of your chosen IDE or model runner to point toward the Jina executable.


### Installing the server package


To run the Jina MCP server locally, you must use the Node package runner to execute the official server package. You can initiate the server by running` npx -y @jina-ai/mcp-server` in your terminal, which fetches the latest version of the Jina Reader MCP implementation.


This command serves as the bridge that exposes the` read` and` search` tools to your local environment.


### Configuring the desktop client


For users on Claude Desktop, this requires adding a` jina-reader` entry to the` mcpServers` object within the` claude_desktop_config.json` file, specifying the command and your API key as an environment variable.


You must set the command to` npx` and include the arguments` -y` ,` @jina-ai/mcp-server` , and your` JINA_API_KEY` to ensure the model can authenticate with the Jina Reader backend.


In Cursor (the AI-native code editor) the integration is handled via the MCP settings pane.


You register the server URL to grant GPT-6.2 Astra or Claude Opus 5.5 direct access to the` search` and` read` tools. Once the handshake is verified, the "Tools" icon in the chat interface will light up.


### Rate limits for free vs pro tiers


Rate limits act as the primary throttle for agentic stability, preventing a recursive loop from triggering an accidental DoS on the target web server.


The free tier provides sufficient requests per minute for manual research sessions. If you're deploying autonomous loops on Gemini 4 Carbon or Grok 4.7, you'll require the Pro tier to avoid` 429 Too Many Requests` errors during deep-crawl operations.
